content.thinking: No `timeout` command. Let me use a Python wrapper with subprocess and a timeout.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - <<'PY'
import subprocess, json, os, time
env=dict(os.environ, PATH="/workspace/tmp/binlink", TMPDIR="/workspace/tmp", PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1")
t=time.time()
p=subprocess.run(["/usr/local/bin/python3","-B","/workspace/submission/main.py"],
                 stdin=open('/workspace/examples/fullwidth.in.json','rb'),
                 stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
print("exit",p.returncode,"%.1fs"%(time.time()-t), p.stderr.decode()[:300])
a=json.loads(p.stdout.decode()); b=json.load(open('/workspace/examples/fullwidth.out.json'))
print("MATCH GOLD" if a==b else ("DIFF", a['cases'][0]['objective'], b['cases'][0]['objective']))
PY
